newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 11.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

An Indonesian court rejected a lawsuit filed by ousted Indonesian Democratic Party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri against the government over her dismissal from the party leadership. Megawati was ousted from the leadership by a government-backed congress called by a rival party faction in Medan, North Sumatra in June.

Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said that government intervention was crucial for providing economic opportunities to all Indonesians as sometimes capitalism excludes certain sections of society.

The Dutch Ambassador to Indonesia, Paul Brouwer, said allegations that Dutch authorities had mistreated an Indonesian pilot in custody were completely unfounded. The Garuda Indonesia pilot was arrested late last month and is charged with smuggling Ecstasy pills.
President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, said he has no interest in buying a stake in Indonesian car manufacturer PT Astra International.

Timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan said he is interested in buying a stake in automobile manufacturer Astra International on behalf of the Nusamba group he controls. Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto. Hasan and the president's eldest son own 10 percent each.
